name: Digitech Bahamas
primary_cta: Request a site visit (work order: business type, needs, tills, location; sends a prefilled email to sales@digitechbahamas.com); secondary: call (242) 676-2033 / 676-3022
brand_truth: A local Nassau team that installs Razor POS and builds the network, Wi-Fi and cloud backup behind it, then supports it after installation.
buyer: Owners and managers of Nassau restaurants, bars, shops and small offices who fear the till or Wi-Fi going down on a busy night, data loss, and an installer who disappears.

direction.type: T04 Technical mono (Sora + IBM Plex Sans + Plex Mono for callout labels and numbers)
direction.why: Digitech sells physical systems, so the object (one counter with a POS terminal) is explained part by part; limestone ground with one sea-glass accent reads Bahamian and calm instead of a dark 'tech' template.

big_idea: Scrolling X-rays one Nassau counter: the Razor POS till, then the cabling, the multi-VLAN Wi-Fi with firewall and VPN, and the cloud backup behind it, drawn onto the photograph as leader lines.
concept_type: brochure / sales site with enquiry (same kind as their WordPress brochure)
tier_why: Photography plus a scroll-driven X-ray wipe and line drawing (transform and stroke only, no WebGL); 3D would add weight without explaining more.

current_site_findings: All Get Started / Learn More / Read more buttons link to '#'
Theme stock photos, nothing shows their installs
Theme counters ('1426+ Developer Hours') read like a software agency
Directory address/phone (Soldier Road, 393-1249) conflicts with the site (East Avenue, Centreville, 676-2033/3022)
pitch_line: Your site shows stock photos and dead buttons; this one shows a Nassau owner, in ten seconds, everything you build behind their till, and books the site visit.
assumptions: #33 East Avenue, Centreville is the current address (directories still list Soldier Road)
A site visit / survey is how a job starts (category-standard step, not stated on their site)
Design and written quote step is category-standard
All photographs are illustrative (generated); replace with Digitech's own install photos
Client names (Hana, Naughty Johnny's, Blu Sail, Beauty Shack, Little Caesars) appear only as logos on their site, so they were left off; can be added with permission
notes: Gen-2 rebuild by scheduled site worker. Picked over the two queue-top institutions (association, government agency) as an easier SME per the worker brief.
